Subject: Private VPC deployment — quick recap & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned while you evaluate deployment modes (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

Summary of needs you mentioned:
- Must keep model inference traffic inside your AWS account (regulated data)
- Expecting ~60 req/s at peak, avg 30 req/s; 10k tokens/minute
- Prefer private connectivity (no public internet) and company-managed KMS for keys

Our recommendation based on that profile: Private VPC deployment (Redwood Private) via AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering. PrivateLink typically simplifies routing with no cross-account route changes; peering works too if your infra team prefers it.

Network / security checklist (high level):
- Choose connectivity: PrivateLink (recommended) or VPC Peering
- Provide one or more customer subnets / CIDR ranges we can reach (or we provide service SP endpoint)
- IP allowlist / egress IPs (we'll provide stable egress IPs if you need outbound allowlist)
- KMS/HSM integration for model keys (bring-your-own-key supported)
- Audit logs / retention & access controls

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you confirm preferred connectivity (PrivateLink vs Peering) and which AWS account/region this should live in?
2) Share a primary contact from FinMetrics infra (email & calendar availability) so we can schedule a short 30-min network design call with our SEs (Vivek) and Marissa (CS lead).
3) I'll attach a Private Deployment checklist and a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) you can review — Marissa will convert to a formal timeline once we have the CIDR/account details.

Attachments: redwood-private-deployment-checklist.pdf, redwood-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick call if helpful.

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Hi Alex / Sean / Vivek —

Thanks for the details. Per our PrivateLink pattern (Vivek can confirm implementation details) — Redwood publishes a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in our account and exposes a service name that your infra creates an interface endpoint for in your account. High-level notes: 

- Permissions: Your team will need permissions to create com.amazonaws.vpce.interface endpoints and associate security groups to those endpoints. No cross-account route table changes are required.
- Egress IPs: For calls originating from within your VPC to our service, traffic flows over the interface endpoint. For outbound connections we initiate (if any), we provide a small stable set of egress IPs (listed below) that you can allowlist for callbacks/logging: 3.10.45.21, 3.10.45.22, 3.10.45.23. If you prefer to NAT on your side, we can accept that too — just let us know.
- KMS: We support BYOK for model keys; we'll need the key ARN and an IAM role for the cross-account decrypt permission if you want Redwood to use your KMS for tokenization or model inputs.

Draft timeline (estimates):
- Week 0: Confirm connectivity method + share CIDR and primary infra contact
- Week 1: Network design call (30m) + distribution of security docs
- Week 2-3: Endpoint setup & test (PrivateLink)
- Week 4: Internal validation + go-live/hand-off to CS ops

I'll attach a one-page network playbook and will update the MAP with the timeline and owners. Vivek — can you add any implementation notes for the SE playbook?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
